workload.audio: 11.0 s mono 24 kHz real speech (JFK inaugural excerpt, openai/whisper test fixture, ffmpeg-resampled)
workload.prompt: processor-shaped transcription request, 146 prompt tokens, 83 audio frames
workload.generation: greedy, 49 new tokens to natural EOS (<|im_end|>)

hardware: AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ PRO 395, Radeon 8060S (gfx1151), 256-bit LPDDR5X
protocol: same-process lanes, 3 repetitions after warmup, best-of reported; both lanes use the identical normalized PCM and the identical RMS/dB/clip/pad preprocessing; torch lane is transformers eager-attention bf16 on cuda (sdpa unsupported by the tokenizer encoder)

gates.correctness: greedy chain 16/16 equal to torch fixture (test_gpu_vibevoice_qwen2_runner); front-end parity rel 2.1e-3 vs fp32 CPU reference, rel <= 5e-2 vs torch-GPU bf16 fixture; 10/10 gpu-suite tests; E2E transcript content identical to torch (End timestamp 11.0 vs 11.07 - benign bf16 path divergence)

notes: not yet faster than torch end to end (1.03x); hipEngine decode is already faster per token (66-78 ms vs ~81 ms), and the residual gap is prompt prefill (~0.7 s for 146 rows) and front-end (0.35 s vs ~0.30 s torch audio)

front-end optimization retained wins vs first working version: 0.92 s -> 0.35 s (scratch arena instead of per-call malloc, warp-per-row rmsnorm, A&S fast-erf gelu, WMMA bulk GEMM for FFN/connectors where tile-aligned, im2col+WMMA for the five large strided convs)
WMMA GEMV variants were tried for the decode path and measured slower (bulk-tile kernels, rows=1): 7.8 s vs 4.2 s prompt+decode; reverted to the scalar dense GEMV family

torch lane uses eager attention for the whole model because the HF tokenizer encoder does not support sdpa; transformers 5.15.0 get_audio_features crashes on 2-D input_values (upstream chunk-cache bug), worked around with 3-D input
